paper.citation: Zhang, A., Brown, L. D. and Cai, T. T. (2019). Semi-supervised inference: General theory and estimation of means. The Annals of Statistics 47(5), 2538-2566. DOI: 10.1214/18-AOS1756.
paper.title: Semi-supervised inference: General theory and estimation of means
paper.source_version: Actually read arXiv:1606.07268v2 (2018-08-14), 62 pages, linked to the 2019 journal publication. Journal final simulation equations were not independently compared; this contribution claims fidelity to the pinned preprint setting only.
paper.source_locator: Pinned arXiv v2 Section 4, setting 3, PDF p. 19 (unnumbered display); Table 1 on PDF p. 20 supplies (p,n,m)=(10,100,1000); sampling equations (1.1)-(1.2), PDF p. 2. These are preprint PDF page numbers, not journal pages.

mechanism.name: Poisson Covariates and Poisson Response Semi-Supervised Mean

generation_equations.label: Response
generation_equations.expression: X_j iid ~ Poisson(10); Y | X ~ Poisson(10 X_1)

generation_equations.label: Sampling and observed data
generation_equations.expression: Independent units and independent outcome noise. Two iid samples from the same population; fixed group sizes, R indicates observed Y. Export X,R,Y_obs where Y_obs=Y when R=1 and 0 otherwise; n_total=nL+nU.

sampling.dependence: Independent complete-data units; fixed labeled/unlabeled group indicators, not independent Bernoulli indicators. Coordinate dependence is specified in equations.
sampling.n_semantics: n is combined table row count
sampling.predictor_source: No external or oracle predictor supplied. Downstream nuisance regressors must be trained on labeled training folds only; cross-fitting and tuning belong to the later estimator benchmark. No prediction is substituted for Y_obs.

assumptions: Independent individuals; labeled and unlabeled observations have the same covariate law and common complete-data population.
Fixed-size labeling independent of X,Y (two-sample/MCAR design); no MAR selection or distribution shift.
Independent noise as specified; finite second moments; R must mask all uses of Y_obs.

properties.notes: Total input dimension 10; source Section 4 setting 3. Only X1 affects response; other nine coordinates do not. Conditional mean is linear; conditional Poisson variance is 10 X1 (heteroskedastic).

estimand.name: theta = E[Y]
estimand.definition: Superpopulation mean theta=E[Y] under the declared fixed mechanism, shared by labeled and unlabeled samples.

parameters.scenario_origin: Source formula and selected source parameters; declared interface adaptations apply.

truth.expression: Superpopulation mean theta=E[Y] under the declared fixed mechanism, shared by labeled and unlabeled samples.
truth.derivation: Iterated expectation of nested Poisson laws

adaptations: Map the two-sample SS design to one numeric table. API n is total rows, not the paper labeled n; R=1 for labeled rows; Y_obs=0 for R=0 is a sentinel, never a label. Source reference sample sizes are stored separately.
For arbitrary CPU test n, labeled_count=max(1,min(n-1,floor(n*nL_ref/(nL_ref+nU_ref)))); first labeled_count rows form the independent labeled sample. At n=nL_ref+nU_ref the source counts are exact.
Independent NumPy PCG64 implementation; no author code copied; original estimator tuning, fitted predictions, repeated CI experiments and PFN training are outside this DGP collection.
